diagnostic_evidence.quote:
there exists a nonzero quaternion $\qq$ such that
\qq[][-1](\qa[1] + \qa[2])\qq = \qb[1] + \qb[2].
Substituting \eqref{eq:PAIRWISE_SIMILARITY_PROOF_PART_1} into \eqref{eq:SUM_SIMILARITY} yields $\qq[][-1]\qa[2]\qq[] = \qb[2]$, which completes the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof first obtains a quaternion q from the sum-similarity equation, then reuses the symbol q for a newly defined q=q1 q2 with an arbitrary q2 commuting with b1. The sum-similarity equation was not established for this new q, so substituting into it is invalid. A valid proof requires constructing a common conjugator directly, e.g. via the standard rotation argument for two vectors with matching Gram matrices.

failure_location.quote: Set $\qq = \qq[1]\qq[2]$, where $\qq[2]$ is a nonzero quaternion such that $\qb[1]\qq[2] = \qq[2]\qb[1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the flawed construction with a correct proof of the converse, for example by using the fact that two ordered vector pairs with equal lengths and equal inner products are related by a proper rotation.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the pairwise-similarity characterization is invalid, although the lemma itself is true. Later results do not depend on this particular proof, but the characterization is not established as written.
issues.title: Invalid construction in pairwise similarity characterization proof
issues.why_classification: The lemma is true, but the supplied proof contains a substantive logical gap requiring a contained replacement argument; no main result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts equivalence, but the proof only starts from a solution of the original Wahba equation and derives the perpendicular-component equation. It never proves the converse, i.e. that any q satisfying the perpendicular-component equation necessarily satisfies the original two equations. The converse is true but requires an additional argument using the pairwise-similarity condition and the fact that conjugation by q is a rotation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a proof of the converse: from the two perpendicular-component equalities, use the rotation action and the pairwise-similarity condition to recover q^{-1}(Im a2)q = Im b2.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is not fully proved as stated. The forward direction used later is valid, but the stated equivalence is unsupported.
issues.title: Only one direction of equivalence proved in perpendicular-component lemma
issues.why_classification: The missing direction is a short contained argument and does not invalidate the later use of the forward implication.

issues.failure_explanation: To preserve the first alignment q^{-1}a1 q = b1, the factor q2 must commute with b1. The proof derives this, but after substituting the general Sylvester solution for q2 it checks q2 b1 = b1 q2 and drops the lambda2 square-root term, only constraining mu2. When a3 = -b3 and a3 != 0, the argument a3 b3^* is negative real, so its square root can be any pure unit. The stated condition a3·Im q2 = 0 only forces Im q2 perpendicular to a3, not parallel to b1, so it allows q2 that do not commute with b1. For example, take a1=b1=i, a2=-k, b2=k, q1=1, q2=k. Then a3=j, b3=-j, the condition j·k=0 holds, but q=k gives |k^{-1} i k - i|^2 = 4, so it is not a solution. The formula also uses q1^* instead of q1^{-1}, further misstating the needed condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing condition that q2 commutes with b1 (equivalently, choose the square root in the centralizer of b1), and correct the q1^* scaling/condition in the q2 formula.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed closed-form parameterization of all solutions is not a set of solutions; it includes quaternions that fail Wahba's equation. The main theorem is invalid as stated.
issues.title: General Wahba solution formula overgenerates non-solutions
issues.why_classification: The main general-solution theorem is false as written and includes non-solutions; repairing it requires a substantive correction of the central parameterization.

issues.failure_explanation: If Im a1 and Im a2 are parallel, then a1×a2=0 and b1×b2=0. The theorem's q2 formula becomes lambda2 sqrt(0), hence q2=0, so q=0, which is not a valid solution because q^{-1} is undefined. The proof also applies the Sylvester-solution theorem to a3=b3=0, outside its nonreal/similarity hypotheses. The correct solution in this case is q=q1 q2 with q2 any nonzero quaternion commuting with b1, or simply any solution of the first alignment, since the second equation is then automatic. For example, a1=b1=i and a2=b2=2i are pairwise similar and q=1 solves the Wahba equation, but the theorem gives q2=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle the case a1×a2=0 separately, setting q2 to an arbitrary nonzero quaternion commuting with b1 (or equivalently taking q=q1 q2 with q2 in the centralizer of b1).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed general solution fails completely for the valid case of parallel observations.
issues.title: Parallel observation case gives q2=0 and misses all solutions
issues.why_classification: This is a degenerate case that can be fixed by a short separate case distinction while preserving the advertised scope and method.
